title: The Viper and the File
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Viper entered a carpenter's shop, and went from one to another of the tools, begging for something to eat. Among the rest, he addressed himself to the File, and asked for the favour of a meal. The File replied in a tone of pitying contempt, "What a simpleton you must be if you imagine you will get anything from me, who invariably take from every one and never give anything in return." The covetous are poor givers.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did the Viper enter?
According to the passage, what was the Viper doing as he moved among the tools?
options: Looking for a place to hide

questions.prompt: According to the passage, which tool did the Viper ask for the favour of a meal?
According to the passage, in what tone did the File reply to the Viper?
As the passage uses it, what does "simpleton" mean in "What a simpleton you must be"?
As the passage uses it, what does "covetous" mean in "The covetous are poor givers"?
Based on the passage, why is it especially foolish for the Viper to expect food from the File?
options: A file's very nature is to take material away, never to provide anything
The File is too small to notice him
The File already gave away all its food

questions.prompt: Which statement, made explicit at the end of the passage, best captures the point of the fable?
options: Carpenters should keep a closer watch on their tools
Tools are more useful than food

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Viper do before addressing the File?
options: He slept beside the tools overnight
He went from one tool to another, begging

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what exactly did the Viper ask the File for?
According to the passage, what does the File say it invariably does?
options: Takes from everyone and never gives in return

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "invariably" mean in "who invariably take from every one"?
Based on the passage, what does the File's blunt reply reveal about it, compared to a hypocrite?
options: It secretly wants to help the Viper but cannot
It is ashamed of how it treats others
It plans to change its ways after this encounter
It openly admits its own selfish nature rather than pretending to be generous

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Viper enters a shop and easily gets fed by a friendly Hammer
A carpenter chases a Viper out of his shop
A hungry Viper begs a File for food, but the File bluntly says it only takes and never gives
A File begs a Viper for food and is refused
